# plugin-runner

Runs a build plugin from `plugins/<name>.sh`.

```
node src/launcher.mjs <name> [args...]
```

The launcher exits with the plugin's own exit code. When the plugin cannot be
run it must **refuse**: exit code `2`, with a message on stderr naming the
plugin. Refusing is not the same as letting the shell fail -- a refusal means the
plugin was never started.

content.text:
All tests pass.

**Fix:** `runPlugin` in `src/launcher.mjs` only checked `existsSync`, which is true for directories too — pointing a "plugin" at a directory (or anything non-file) let `spawnSync` run bash against it, so the guard didn't actually refuse, it let the shell fail on its own with whatever exit code bash chose. Now it `statSync`s the path and requires `isFile()`, checks read access with `accessSync`, and also catches `spawnSync`'s own `run.error` (failed-to-spawn case) — all three paths refuse via a shared `refuse(name, reason)` helper that writes `plugin <name> <reason>` to stderr and returns exit code 2, *before* bash is ever invoked.

Working and legitimately-failing plugins are untouched: `hello` still exits 0, `fails` still propagates its exit code 7.

**Tests added:** a directory named `<plugin>.sh` is now refused with exit 2 and a stderr message naming the plugin, verified via a temp scratch dir. All 4 tests (3 original + 1 new) pass.
